name: Reubenites
overview: The Reubenites, descendants of Israel's eldest son Reuben, were a significant tribe in Israel's military organization, as evidenced by their enrollment at Mount Sinai with over forty-six thousand men able to go to war (Numbers 1:20-21). They held a strategic position in the camp and march, with their standard set on the south side under the leadership of Elizur son of Shedeur (Numbers 2:10; 10:18). Their families were numerous, numbering over forty-three thousand in later counts (Numbers 26:7), and they played a role in the conquest of territories east of the Jordan River, including battles such as the one against King Og of Bashan at Edrei (Deuteronomy 3:1).
